Prior Distribution Constructors for Sensitivity Analysis

Source: R/priors.R
bf_priors.Rd

Backend-agnostic prior specification functions for use with sensitivity_plot, ecdf_model_plot, ecdf_prior_plot and overall_plot. These create lightweight prior objects that are translated to the format each model backend expects. A prior a backend cannot fit exactly is an error, never a silent substitution.

Usage

bf_normal(mean = 0, sd = 1)

bf_student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1)

bf_half_normal(mean = 0, sd = 1)

bf_half_cauchy(location = 0, scale = 1)

bf_half_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1)

bf_exponential(rate = 1)

bf_lognormal(meanlog = 0, sdlog = 1)

bf_uniform(lower = 0, upper = 1)

Arguments

mean, location

Prior mean or location parameter.

sd, scale

Prior standard deviation or scale parameter.

df

Degrees of freedom.

rate

Rate parameter (for bf_exponential only).

meanlog, sdlog

Mean and standard deviation of \(\log(\tau)\) (for bf_lognormal only).

lower, upper

Bounds of the uniform prior. For \(\tau\), lower must be 0.

Value

An object of class "bf_prior" containing the distribution family and parameters.

Details

Priors for the pooled effect (\(\mu\)) are on the model scale (the log scale for OR, RR, HR and IRR). Priors for the heterogeneity (\(\tau\)) are on the standard deviation of the study effects.

Priors for \(\mu\)

bf_normal(mean, sd)

Normal distribution.

bf_student_t(df, location, scale)

Student-t distribution: a heavier-tailed, weakly informative alternative to the normal. df = 1 is a Cauchy distribution.

Priors for \(\tau\)

bf_half_normal(mean, sd)

Half-normal distribution (truncated at 0).

bf_half_cauchy(location, scale)

Half-Cauchy distribution.

bf_half_t(df, location, scale)

Half-Student-t distribution.

bf_exponential(rate)

Exponential distribution.

bf_lognormal(meanlog, sdlog)

Log-normal distribution. Use bf_turner for the empirical priors of Turner et al.

bf_uniform(0, upper)

Uniform distribution from 0 to upper.

bf_rhodes()

Empirical log-t priors of Rhodes et al.

Backend support

Sensitivity refits stop with an error if the model's backend cannot fit a prior exactly:

PriorbrmsbayesmetaMetaStan
bf_normal (\(\mu\))yesyesyes
bf_student_t (\(\mu\))yesnono
bf_half_normalyesyesyes (mean 0)
bf_half_cauchyyesyesyes (location 0)
bf_half_tyesyesno
bf_exponentialyesyesno
bf_lognormal, bf_turneryesyesno
bf_uniformyesyesyes
bf_rhodesyesyesno

Priors cannot be changed for rstan, cmdstanr, rstanarm, bayesma, RoBMA or JAGS models.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
priors <- list(
  vague = list(
    name      = "Vague",
    mu_prior  = bf_normal(0, 10),
    tau_prior = bf_half_cauchy(0, 1)
  ),
  weakreg = list(
    name      = "Weakly Regularising",
    mu_prior  = bf_student_t(3, 0, 1),
    tau_prior = bf_half_normal(0, 0.5)
  ),
  empirical = list(
    name      = "Empirical (Turner)",
    mu_prior  = bf_normal(0, 1),
    tau_prior = bf_turner("all-cause mortality",
                          "pharmacological", "placebo / control")
  )
)

sensitivity_plot(model, data, priors = priors, measure = "OR")
} # }
